features.name: Basic arithmetic and expression evaluation
steps: Enter numbers from a blank state
Perform +, -, ×, ÷ separately
Tap = to get the correct result
Enter an expression with several operators, e.g. 2 + 3 × 4
Compute with the correct operator precedence
After getting a result, continue entering operators and numbers to keep calculating from the current result. Integers, decimals, chained operations, and the result state must be handled correctly.
features.expected: The four basic operations must give correct results; multi-operator expressions follow the correct precedence, e.g. 2 + 3 × 4 should be 14; results can continue into further operations; integer and decimal precision is reasonable.

features.name: Clearing, character-by-character deletion, and the calculation state
steps: Enter a multi-digit number or an unfinished expression
Tap C
Delete one character of the current input
Tap repeatedly to delete character by character
Long-press C
Clear the entire calculation state and restore the initial 0
After completing a calculation, entering a new number correctly starts a new calculation state.
features.expected: C deletes one character of the current input each time; long-pressing C clears the entire calculation state and restores the initial 0; after completing a calculation, entering a new number starts a new calculation state without leaving the old expression behind.

features.name: Percentage, square root, and power
steps: Use % for percentage calculations
Use √ to take the square root of a positive number
Use ^ to enter the base and exponent for exponentiation
The results of special operations can continue into + - × ÷
Decimal results keep reasonable precision
Invalid operations must not push the UI into an error state.
features.expected: Percentage, square-root, and power operations give correct results; invalid operations such as the square root of a negative number give feedback without crashing; results can continue into arithmetic; decimal results keep reasonable precision.

features.name: History
steps: Complete several groups of different expressions in succession
Tap the history button at the top
The "History" window pops up
Each entry shows the original expression and its result
The current calculation state is preserved after closing the window
New calculations continue to be added to the history
Tap "Clear" to delete the history
Reopening the history verifies that the records have been cleared.
features.expected: The history records the original expressions and their results in order; the current calculation state is preserved after closing the history window; new calculations continue to be added; after tapping clear the records are empty and do not come back after a restart.

features.name: Length unit conversion
steps: Open "Unit converter"
Enter "Length"
Select units on both sides separately
Enter a number on either side and the other converts in real time
Changing either side's unit recalculates immediately
Tap the central swap button to exchange the source/target units

Verify decimal, large-number, and cross-order-of-magnitude results. All 16 units must be provided: kilometer (km), meter (m), centimeter (cm), millimeter (mm), micrometer (μm), nanometer (nm), ångström (Å), mile (mi), yard (yd), foot (ft), inch (in), fathom, nautical mile (NM), astronomical unit (au), parsec (pc), and light-year (ly).
features.expected: The units on both sides can be selected independently; entering a value on either side converts the other in real time; the swap button exchanges the source and target units; the conversions match the standard, e.g. 1 km = 1000 m; all 16 units exist.

features.name: Area unit conversion
steps: Enter "Area"
Enter an area in any source unit
The target area shows the converted value in real time
Switch between metric square units, British/American square units, and land-area units
Verify square multipliers rather than ordinary length multipliers

Use the swap button to convert in reverse. All 10 units must be provided: square kilometer (km²), square meter (m²), square centimeter (cm²), square millimeter (mm²), square mile (sq mi), square yard (sq yd), square foot (sq ft), square inch (sq in), acre (ac), and hectare (ha).
features.expected: Square units use square multipliers rather than length multipliers, e.g. 1 m² = 10000 cm²; metric, British/American, and land units are all selectable; the swap button gives correct reverse results; all 10 units exist.

features.name: Volume and capacity unit conversion
steps: Enter "Volume"
Enter a numeric value
Switch between cubic metric, liter-based capacity, US capacity, and imperial capacity
Verify that US/imperial units with the same name, such as gallon, quart, and pint, have different conversion factors
Tap the swap button to convert in reverse

Continue verifying with decimals. All 25 units must be provided: cubic meter (m³), cubic decimeter (dm³), cubic centimeter (cm³), cubic millimeter (mm³), liter (L), centiliter (cL), deciliter (dL), milliliter (mL), acre-foot (ac ft), cubic foot (ft³), cubic inch (in³), barrel [US] (fl bl (US)), gallon [US] (gal (US)), quart [US] (qt (US)), pint [US] (pt (US fl)), cup [US] (cup (US)), gill [US] (gi (US)), fluid ounce [US] (US fl oz), barrel [imp] (bl (imp)), gallon [imp] (gal (imp)), quart [imp] (qt (imp)), pint [imp] (pt (imp)), gill [imp] (gi (imp)), and fluid ounce [imp] (fl oz (imp)).
features.expected: US and imperial units with the same name have different conversion factors; entering a value on either side updates the other in real time; the swap button gives consistent reverse results; all 25 units exist.

features.name: Mass unit conversion
steps: Enter "Mass"
Enter a mass value
Switch between metric, imperial/US, and traditional mass units
Verify smaller and larger orders of magnitude
It updates in real time when the target unit changes

Swap the source and target units. All 14 units must be provided: gram (g), kilogram (kg), milligram (mg), microgram (μm), metric ton (t), pound (lb), ounce (oz), grain (gr), dram (dr), stone (st), long ton (ton), short ton (sh tn), karat (kt), and metric carat (ct).
features.expected: Metric-to-imperial conversions are correct, e.g. 1 kg = 1000 g; results are correct for both large and small magnitudes; the swap button converts in reverse; all 14 units exist.

features.name: Temperature unit conversion
steps: Enter "Temperature"
Select different temperature scales in the upper and lower areas
Enter a positive temperature to get a real-time result
Use +/- to enter negative numbers
Switch between the temperature scales
Verify that temperature conversion correctly handles scale and zero-point offset, e.g. 0°C
After swapping the units on both sides the conversion works in reverse. All 4 units must be provided: Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F), Rankine (°R), and Kelvin (K).
features.expected: Temperature conversion correctly handles scale and zero-point offset, e.g. 0°C should be 273.15 K; negative input is supported; after swapping, the reverse result is correct; all 4 temperature scales exist.

features.name: Time unit conversion
steps: Enter "Time"
Enter a numeric value
Switch between different time scales
Verify conversions across orders of magnitude from milliseconds to years
Enter a decimal
It updates in real time when the unit changes
Use the swap button to convert in reverse. All 7 units must be provided: hour (h), minute (m), second (s), millisecond (ms), day (d), week (wk), and year (y).
features.expected: Conversions across orders of magnitude from milliseconds to years are correct; decimal results are reasonable; changing a unit updates the other side in real time; the swap button converts in reverse; all 7 units exist.

features.name: Speed unit conversion
steps: Enter "Speed"
Convert between common traffic speed units
Then test high-speed/scientific units
Enter decimals and larger values
Changing the upper/lower units recomputes in real time
Swap the units. All 8 units must be provided: meter/second (m/s), kilometer/second (km/s), kilometer/hour (km/h), mile/hour (mph), knot (kn), foot/second (ft/s), Mach (Ma), and speed of light (c).
features.expected: Common and scientific speed conversions are correct, e.g. 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h; results are reasonable for both small and large values; the swap button converts in reverse; all 8 units exist.

features.name: Pressure unit conversion
steps: Enter "Pressure"
Convert between SI pressure units, bar/atm, and mercury units
After entering a value, switch the target unit in turn
Verify that the results refresh automatically

Swap the units on both sides to verify the reverse calculation. All 10 units must be provided: pascal (Pa), kilopascal (kPa), megapascal (MPa), bar, millibar (mbar), atmosphere (atm), pound per square inch (psi), torr (Torr), millimeter of mercury (mmHg), and inch of mercury (inHg).
features.expected: The conversion relationships among SI, bar, atm, and mercury units are correct, e.g. 1 atm = 101325 Pa; switching the target unit refreshes the result automatically; after swapping, the reverse result is consistent; all 10 units exist.

features.name: Energy unit conversion
steps: Enter "Energy"
Enter an energy value
Switch between SI, heat, watt-hour, electrical, and traditional units
Verify very large/very small multipliers
Use decimals
Swap the source and target units

The results stay consistent. All 14 units must be provided: joule (J), kilojoule (kJ), megajoule (MJ), gigajoule (GJ), calorie (cal), kilocalorie (kcal), watt-hour (Wh), kilowatt-hour (kWh), megawatt-hour (MWh), electronvolt (eV), British thermal unit (BTU), therm (thm), foot-pound (ft⋅lbf), and erg (erg).
features.expected: The conversion relationships among SI, heat, watt-hour, and electrical units are correct, e.g. 1 kWh = 3600000 J; extremely large or small magnitudes give reasonable results; the swap button converts in reverse; all 14 units exist.

features.name: Uniform interaction and state switching across the nine conversion categories
steps: From the unit-converter home, enter Length, Area, Volume, Mass, Temperature, Time, Speed, Pressure, and Energy in turn
Every page keeps the unified pattern of "source unit on top + target unit below + numeric keypad + central swap button"
Returning from one category and entering another must not mix in the wrong dimension
Each category uses its own set of valid units
Input values, clearing, and decimal behavior are consistent.
features.expected: All nine categories keep a uniform input and swap interaction; each category uses its own valid unit set without mixing dimensions; when returning and entering another category the input value initializes correctly; clearing and decimal behavior are consistent.

features.name: Appearance, themes, and fonts
steps: The menu in the top-right corner
Settings
Custom appearance
Change the app theme
Change the app icon color
Change the app font
Return to the main calculator and observe the UI changes
Then enter the unit-conversion page and the theme stays consistent
The settings are still preserved after restarting/re-entering.
features.expected: Theme, icon-color, and font changes take effect immediately on the calculator and converter pages; the settings persist after a restart; switching themes must not clear the existing calculation state or history.

features.name: Widget color customization
steps: Settings
"Custom widget color"
Open the widget preview
Change the foreground/background related colors
Move the slider and observe the preview changing immediately
Tap "OK" to save
Re-entering the settings verifies that the color value is preserved.
features.expected: The preview updates immediately while dragging the slider; after confirming the color value is saved and re-entering the settings shows the saved value; cancelling must not save the changes.

features.name: Key vibration and keeping the device awake in the foreground
steps: Toggle "vibrate when pressing buttons" in the settings
Return to the calculator to operate digits and operators
The vibration behavior changes according to the setting
Toggle "prevent the device from sleeping while the app is in the foreground"
Return to the calculator and converter screens
The settings should persist across pages without affecting the existing history or calculation state.
features.expected: The vibration setting genuinely affects key feedback; the prevent-sleep setting takes effect on both the calculator and converter pages; the settings persist across pages without affecting history or the calculation state.
